issues.legal_issue: A condition in a conveyance of an industrial plot requiring timely establishment of an industrial unit, with resumption for non-compliance, is not invalid merely because it restricts the transferee’s use of the property.
material_facts: The plot was conveyed for industrial use under an agreement requiring construction of a building and commencement of production within specified periods, failing which the plot could be resumed.
The allottee did not establish the industrial unit and, in response to a show-cause notice, referred to difficulties with power and water and said the scheme had been abandoned.
The allottee contended that the condition was unenforceable because it restricted the use of the property transferred.
issues.conclusion: The condition was valid; the conveyance did not create an absolute interest to which the restriction was repugnant.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 11 of the Transfer of Property Act, a restriction repugnant to an absolute interest may be void, but the conveyance here did not create an absolute interest. Sections 31 and 32 permit an interest to be made subject to a valid condition that it cease on the happening or non-happening of a specified uncertain event. The condition that an industrial unit be established within the stipulated period was valid.

predicates.challenge_to_contractual_resumption: A proceeding challenges resumption of property under a contractual condition.
predicates.conditional_interest_created: The transfer makes the recipient’s interest subject to a condition that it may cease if a specified event does or does not occur.
predicates.industrial_unit_not_established: The recipient does not establish the industrial unit required by the transfer arrangement.
predicates.industrial_use_condition_is_valid: The condition requiring industrial use and permitting resumption for non-compliance is legally valid.

issues.definition: When a proceeding challenges contractual resumption and the transferred interest is conditional, failure to establish the required industrial unit means the industrial-use condition is valid.

issues.legal_issue: An assignee of rights under a contract involving mutual obligations cannot, without the other contracting party’s consent, require that party to recognize the assignee or allow the assignee to challenge resumption based on the contract.
material_facts: The allottee transferred its rights in the plot to the petitioner while the suit challenging resumption was pending, and the petitioner was added as a plaintiff.
The agreement between the allottee and the corporation imposed reciprocal obligations, including the obligation to establish an industrial unit.
The corporation had entered the agreement in reliance on the allottee’s undertaking and its perceived ability to perform.
The corporation did not consent to the transfer or agree to recognize the petitioner as the allottee.
issues.conclusion: The petitioner had no locus standi to challenge the resumption order, and the transfer did not require the corporation to recognize her as the allottee.
issues.legal_principle: An assignment may transfer contractual rights, but obligations generally cannot be assigned without the promisee’s consent; where consent is given, the result may be a novation. A right under a contract involving mutual rights and obligations cannot be enforced by an assignee without fulfilment of the correlative obligations. The Court relied on Halsbury’s Laws of England, Fourth Edition, Part 9, paragraph 337, and Khardah Company Ltd. v. Raymon and Co. (India) Pvt. Ltd., AIR 1962 SC 1810. The transfer pendente lite was not barred by Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, but that did not give the assignee the contractual standing she claimed.

predicates.assignee_challenges_resumption: A person who acquired contractual rights from an allottee seeks to challenge resumption of the allotted property.
predicates.mutual_contract_obligations: The contract imposes reciprocal obligations on the allottee and the other contracting party.
predicates.assignment_without_consent: The allottee transfers its contractual position without the other contracting party’s consent.
predicates.assignee_lacks_standing_to_challenge_res: The assignee cannot require recognition as the allottee or challenge the contractual resumption.

issues.definition: When an assignee challenges resumption under a contract involving reciprocal obligations and the assignment lacked the other party’s consent, the assignee lacks standing to challenge that resumption.
